title.es: Club de lectura: la gran discusión

es: Debatir una historia: interpretar un final, defenderlo con dos deducciones, valorarlo y aceptar una lectura distinta con educación.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención en el club de lectura: lectura, pruebas, concesión y cierre.

answer.text: I would argue that the ending of The Blue Door is ambiguous on purpose. The narrator says that nobody ever lived in the house, but he can't have been honest, because he also says that his sister left after an argument. The wet letter is a clue: she must have written it in a hurry, and he might have hidden it for years. In my reading, the blue door is a symbol of a memory that he cannot close. Carlos thinks the narrator is lying to us, and I concede that this is plausible. However, I am not convinced that the book wants us to be certain. The writer hides an important detail in a subtle way, and the imagery of cold and rain makes the sadness resonate with readers. It is a thoughtful novel, although the pacing is slow in the middle, and I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys a gripping story with a difficult ending. Fair enough, Carlos: we will have to agree to disagree.

Carlos thinks the narrator is lying to us, and I concede that this is plausible. However, I am not convinced that the book wants us to be certain. The writer hides an important detail in a subtle way, and the imagery of cold and rain makes the sadness resonate with readers. It is a thoughtful novel, although the pacing is slow in the middle, and I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys a gripping story with a difficult ending. Fair enough, Carlos: we will have to agree to disagree.

I would argue that the last scene is ambiguous, and I read it as a symbol of memory. The narrator can't have been telling the whole truth, because the letter was wet, so someone must have read it or hidden it. His sister might have left in anger, and he might have closed the blue door to forget her. Carlos says that the narrator is lying, and I concede that this is plausible, because the clues contradict him. Even so, I am not convinced that the writer wants a clear answer. The cold imagery conveys sadness, and the ending will resonate with anyone who has lost someone. It is a thoughtful book, although the pacing is slow. You make a fair point, Carlos, but we will have to agree to disagree.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención propone una lectura, la apoya con dos deducciones, admite el punto del otro y cierra con respeto.

origin.text: Club de lectura. La novela «The Blue Door» termina así: el narrador cierra la puerta azul de la casa y dice «Nobody ever lived here». Antes contó que su hermana se fue tras una discusión y que la carta de ella apareció mojada. Escribe tu intervención (entre 120 y 200 palabras): interpreta el final con I would argue that…, defiéndelo con dos deducciones (must have, can't have, might have) apoyadas en pistas, usa un símbolo o imaginería, admite con I concede that… la lectura de Carlos (el narrador miente) y cierra con respeto.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dice la hablante del final.

choices.text: It proves that the narrator lied.
It can be read in more than one way.

feedback.es: Dos lecturas igual de verosímiles y ninguna confirmada: la hablante describe un final abierto.

origin.audio: Some readers say the narrator lied, and others say he was only afraid. Both readings make sense, and the book never says which is right. That is why the ending is so ambiguous.

prompt.es: Carlos presenta otra lectura. ¿Qué respuesta cede con tacto sin rendirse?

choices.text: I see your point, but I read the ending differently.
You are wrong, and that is the end of it.
I agree with everything you say.

feedback.es: Reconocer el punto del otro y mantener tu lectura es ceder con educación sin abandonar tu postura.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es verosímil que ella supiera la verdad, porque nunca hizo preguntas.»

feedback.es: Plausible dice que algo es creíble según las pruebas, sin afirmarlo con seguridad.

origin.text: It is ___ that she knew the truth, because she never asked any questions.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Admito que tus pruebas son convincentes.»

answer.text: I concede that your evidence is convincing

feedback.es: Concede + that introduce lo que admites, aunque no cambies de postura.

prompt.es: ¿Qué término describe un detalle que anuncia lo que vendrá?

feedback.es: El foreshadowing anticipa acontecimientos posteriores; imagery crea atmósfera y plot es el argumento.

I admit that it is possible, but I would argue that the ending is ambiguous.

feedback.es: Se concede el punto con I concede that y se mantiene la lectura con but y ambiguous.

origin.text: Un compañero dice que el narrador miente. Tú admites que es verosímil, pero sigues pensando que el final es ambiguo.
